item.description: INTRODUCTION: Mild neurocognitive disorder (mild NCD) is a clinically relevant stage of cognitive decline with heterogeneous clinical trajectories that remain poorly characterized, limiting efforts to identify early markers of disease progression. It may be associated with structural, functional, metabolic, CSF-related, and molecular features of the brain. item.description: The pharmaceutical landscape is witnessing a profound "Peptide Renaissance," driven primarily by the clinical success of GLP-1 receptor agonists and reinforced by engineering advanced drug delivery platforms. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of current trends in peptide-based drug development, using a target-localization framework that distinguishes molecular recognition from pharmacological action. We delineate the functional divergence between extracellular, cell-surface, and...

item.title: Impact of implementing a specialized rehabilitation hospital system on healthcare utilization in patients with traumatic brain injury: a nationwide retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of the specialized rehabilitation hospital system was associated with increased healthcare utilization and changes in post-acute healthcare utilization pathways among patients with TBI. These findings provide evidence regarding changes in healthcare utilization following implementation of the system.

item.description: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates lesions like tumors via reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative damage. However, tumors overexpress reactive sulfur species (RSS) that scavenge cytotoxic ROS, endowing cancer cells with strong antioxidant resistance and weakening PDT efficacy. We fabricated a biosafe, readily available activatable photosensitizer ST-DNBS based on safranine T (ST). item.title: Association of Concomitant Proton Pump Inhibitor Use with Survival Outcomes During CDK4/6 Inhibitor Therapy for Breast Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant PPI use was associated with shorter rwPFS and OS among patients who remained alive and event-free through day 90. Residual confounding, including differences in the indications for PPI use, may contribute to these associations. Further studies are needed to clarify their clinical significance.

item.title: Longitudinal Clinical Outcomes After Intra-Articular Dexamethasone-Lidocaine Injection for Temporomandibular Joint Arthralgia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intra-articular dexamethasone-lidocaine injection was followed by decreases in pain intensity and pain-location burden and a modest increase in CMO, whereas MMO showed no consistent longitudinal change. These findings support a multidomain approach to assessing clinical trajectories after TMJ injection.

item.description: The location of visual stimuli influences the actions animals select, reflecting the distinct ecological and behavioral significance of the upper and lower visual fields. In mice, the superior colliculus transforms visual information into defensive and approach behaviors, with its superficial layers containing genetically defined cell types with distinct projections. Whether these circuits are repeated across visual space or are specialized by visual-field position remains unclear. Dual-color...

item.title: Tezepelumab for asthma-COPD coexistence receiving long-term oxygen therapy: Two cases
item.description: Asthma-COPD coexistence is associated with frequent exacerbations that worsen patients' quality of life. Although tezepelumab, an anti-thymic stromal lymphopoietin monoclonal antibody, is effective in preventing exacerbations in severe asthma, evidence of its efficacy in asthma-COPD coexistence is limited. We describe two elderly former smokers with asthma-COPD coexistence receiving long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) who remained symptomatic despite inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting...

item.title: TaPaD: An instance-level image dataset for tactile paving with deterioration annotations
item.description: Tactile paving provides navigational cues for people with visual impairments, but its surfaces can deteriorate through cracking, soiling, fading, heat deformation, and wear. This data article presents TaPaD, an instance-level road-surface image dataset for tactile-paving detection, block-type classification, and deterioration assessment. TaPaD contains 1611 images captured with a bicycle-mounted compact camera and 3192 images captured with smartphones. All bicycle images are annotated,...

item.description: Atomically precise titanium-oxo clusters are discrete molecular analogues of TiO(2) and structural building blocks of many metal-organic frameworks. Combining features of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, they provide a versatile platform for catalyst design. However, due to limited stability in aqueous media, they remain largely unexplored in biologically relevant catalysis. item.title: ANCA-Negative Pauci-Immune Crescentic Glomerulonephritis With Atypical Endothelial Injury in a Patient With Long-Standing Rheumatoid Arthritis
item.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic inflammatory disorder that may be complicated by diverse extra-articular manifestations, including renal involvement. Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) is an important cause of crescentic glomerulonephritis; however, ANCA-negative pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in patients with RA is uncommon and diagnostically challenging. We herein report a case of ANCA-negative pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis...

item.title: Subgenome-Resolved Assembly of the Mahseer Tor tambra Reveals Allotetraploid Subgenomes Shared with Tor sinensis
item.description: Mahseers (Tor spp.) are cyprinids of high conservation and aquaculture value, and their genomes carry extensive gene duplication. Whether this duplication reflects 2 subgenomes has not been resolved at chromosome scale. We assembled a 1.76-Gb genome of a wild female Tor tambra from southern Thailand using Oxford Nanopore and Omni-C data. K-mer spectra were best fitted by a tetraploid model with a monoploid size of 0.85 Gb. Alignment to both subgenomes of Tor sinensis revealed 30 Hi-C joins...

item.title: A national environmental scan of postvention services in Veterans Affairs healthcare systems
item.description: CONCLUSION: VA postvention programs varied considerably in structure and scope, though proactive advance planning and outreach to both loved ones and staff were common features. Future implementation efforts could include assisting facilities with documenting their postvention preparation plans in written SOPs, broadening interdisciplinary engagement in providing postvention services, and engaging leadership support.

item.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This integrative systems-immunology framework delineates immune-inflammatory signatures at the PFAS-COPD interface and identifies HMOX1, JUNB, CXCL12, and PTGS2 as convergent molecular nodes. The findings do not establish exposure causality but provide a multi-scale basis for future epidemiological and mechanistic studies of how persistent environmental pollutants may contribute to COPD-associated immune and inflammatory alterations.

item.title: SEVI fibrils are induced by bacterial surface molecules and exert antimicrobial activity against ESKAPE pathogens
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Semen-derived enhancer of viral infection (SEVI) is an amyloid fibril formed from PAP248-286, a fragment of prostatic acid phosphatase naturally occuring in seminal plasma. Beyond its role in HIV transmission, SEVI may contribute to innate immunity. Since many amyloids display antimicrobial effects, we investigated its antibacterial activity against ESKAPE pathogens and urogenital bacteria.

item.title: DASH diet adherence is associated with lower ischemic stroke incidence among older women: findings from a sex-specific analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher DASH adherence was associated with a lower risk of ischemic stroke among older women. These findings support a potential role for the DASH dietary pattern in ischemic stroke prevention and highlight the need for further investigation of sex-specific associations.

item.title: Protective effects of AKBA against hypoxia-induced cognitive dysfunction: potential involvement of SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1
item.description: CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that concurrent AKBA administration provides protection against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction, potentially involving coordinated changes in inflammatory, antioxidant, and neurotrophic responses. However, the causal roles of the candidate proteins and gut microbiota alterations remain to be established through further functional investigations.

item.title: Trajectories of odor identification during and after a 5-year exercise intervention in older adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: OI decline did not differ between the MICT, HIIT, and control groups. However, higher VO(2peak) at baseline and 10 years later was associated with better OI performance. These findings suggest a direct link between VO(2peak) and reduced age-related OI decline in older adults.

item.description: INTRODUCTION: In July 2025, the International Patient Organisation for Primary Immunodeficiencies (IPOPI) held its fourth consecutive Global Multi-Stakeholders' Summit, bringing together key stakeholders and experts in primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs) and related fields to discuss current challenges and opportunities for improving patient care.

item.description: The tripeptide Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) is a minimal integrin-binding motif found in multiple extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins. item.title: Deletion of pyrE disrupts pyrimidine de novo synthesis, attenuates virulence, and confers protective immunity as a live attenuated vaccine candidate against Brucella melitensis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that pyrE is essential for pyrimidine synthesis and virulence in Brucella. The ΔpyrE strain represents a safe, immunogenic, and protective vaccine candidate with long-term potential, providing a new strategy for brucellosis control.

item.title: A cross-sectional and longitudinal examination of adolescents' emotion expression flexibility and their self-injurious thoughts and behaviors
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Suicide is a leading cause of death among adolescents worldwide, yet, understanding of risks factors remains unclear. Past studies have shown that emotion regulation (ER) difficulties are associated with self-injurious thoughts and behaviors (SITBs) in teens but the vast majority of this research has focused on assessing broad ER abilities in response to negative emotions (using the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale; DERS) as opposed to the specific ability to flexibly...

item.title: Diagnostic pathways and unmet healthcare needs in rare diseases: a Romanian survey
item.description: Rare disease policy in Europe increasingly emphasises not only timely diagnosis but also the integration of specialist expertise into sustainable national care pathways. We analysed a cross-sectional, network-based online survey conducted in Romania within the ECOU project to describe diagnostic trajectories and principal unmet care needs and to consider their relevance within the evolving European rare disease landscape. item.description: CONCLUSION: This case showed temporary neurological and radiographic improvement after a multimodal non-surgical approach, but it does not establish the efficacy of an individual treatment component or an overall survival benefit.

item.title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. item.title: Immediate early response 3 promotes airway epithelial inflammation and represents a therapeutic target in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for COPD risk prediction and identified IER3 as a candidate mediator of airway epithelial inflammation. Integrated evidence supports its involvement in smoke-induced inflammatory amplification and potential contribution to impaired lung function, highlighting IER3 as a potential therapeutic target warranting further mechanistic and clinical validation.

item.description: Colorectal cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, underscoring the critical need for novel biomarkers and effective therapeutic targets. item.description: CONCLUSION: The randomized scenario comparisons showed differences in perceived responsibility attribution. Because the scenarios jointly varied multiple features, these findings do not isolate the causal effects of AI functionality, human authority, or opportunities to intervene. Ownership and control ratings partly reflected information supplied in the vignettes and therefore cannot establish distinct causal mediating mechanisms or their temporal sequence.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The four-factor model of the Korean BiSS is a reliable and valid measure for assessing people's perceptions, preferences, and habits related to biphasic sleep, which involves nighttime sleep and daytime naps.

The clinical and radiological overlap with tuberculosis (TB), particularly culture-negative pulmonary TB, poses a significant risk of misdiagnosis. item.title: The Jebel Sahaba-Tushka-Wadi Halfa Nexus in the Late Pleistocene Nile Valley
item.description: OBJECTIVES: This paper uses dental and cranial nonmetric data to assess biological homogeneity among three Nile Valley Late Pleistocene (NVLP) samples: Jebel Sahaba, Tushka, and Wadi Halfa. The objective is to confirm previous data aggregation practices, which have been based primarily on assessments of cranial robusticity, and provide a modified approach to biodistance analysis that privileges trait selection based on the most limiting sample within a hypothesis testing framework.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Emergency onlay mesh repair did not compromise long-term patient-reported outcomes compared with elective repair. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: OA protects granulosa cells and ovarian tissue from oxidative stress-induced inflammatory injury by restoring SIRT1 expression and suppressing NF-κB signaling in a SIRT1-dependent manner. item.description: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role. The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, centered on AKT, contributes to this resistance. Current literature examines AKT's downstream consequences in isolation, overlooking their collective...

item.title: Operator-induced reduction of air kerma during backpack-based gamma-ray measurement
item.description: Backpack-based gamma-ray measurement systems are widely used to monitor environmental radiation; however, measurements can be affected by attenuation caused by the operator's body. The present study investigated the effect of operator-induced attenuation on backpack-based gamma-ray measurements. A backpack gamma-ray measurement system equipped with a 7.62 cm × 7.62 cm NaI(Tl) detector was calibrated through experimental measurements and Monte Carlo simulations. The gamma-ray spectra were divided...

item.title: Advancing structural interpretability in multispecies aquatic toxicity prediction through feature-wise conditioning in multimodal graph neural networks
item.description: Ecological risk assessment requires aquatic toxicity estimates for untested chemical-species combinations. Predictive models can combine molecular structure with physicochemical, species, and exposure information to estimate these toxicities. We examined how this integration affects prediction and structural interpretation. Conventional concatenation joins encoded molecular features with other inputs. We compared this with feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), which adjusts molecular features...

item.title: Nationwide monitoring of neurotoxin β-N-methylamino-L-alanine (BMAA) and its isomers in phytoplankton, mussels, and commercial shellfish from Korean coastal waters
item.description: β-N-methylamino-L-alanine (BMAA) is a neurotoxin produced by certain phytoplankton and has attracted attention due to its potential association with neurodegenerative diseases. However, information on its occurrence, bioaccumulation, and transfer to seafood remains limited. This study investigated the nationwide distribution of BMAA and its isomers, 2,4-diaminobutyric acid (DAB) and N-(2-aminoethyl)glycine (AEG), in phytoplankton, mussels, and commercial shellfish from Korean coastal waters and...

item.title: Bovine Serum Albumin-Crosslinked Silk Fibroin-Based Bioink via Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Bone Tissue Engineering
item.description: CONCLUSION: The Silk-NB/BSA-SH thiol-ene click chemistry bioink presents a design strategy that simultaneously satisfies printability, mechanical performance, and biological functionality. This protein-based functional crosslinking approach addresses key limitations of conventional Sil-MA and supports the potential of the Silk-NB/BSA-SH bioink for digital light processing (DLP)-based bone tissue engineering applications.

item.title: Exposure to Diesel Particulate Matter Aggravates Developmental Toxicity Induced by Cyclophosphamide in Rats
item.description: Despite widespread human exposure to diesel particulate matter (DPM) and its recognized health risks, its impact on embryo-fetal development, particularly under conditions of concomitant exposure to developmental toxicants, remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated whether DPM exacerbates cyclophosphamide (CP)-induced embryo-fetal developmental toxicity in rats and assessed maternal hepatic oxidative stress-related parameters, including malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and...

item.title: Multi-gene phylogeny and morphological study reveal three new species of Ophiostoma Syd. and P. Syd. (Ascomycota, Ophiostomatales) from oak trees in South Korea
item.description: During a survey of putative fungal pathogens infecting oak trees in the Republic of Korea, fungal isolates exhibiting morphological characteristics of Ophiostoma species were consistently collected from natural wounds on oak trees. Based on morphological characterization and phylogenetic analyses, including single-gene phylogenies of ITS, TUB2, TEF1-α, and RPBII sequences, alongside a multi-gene phylogeny of ITS, TUB2, and TEF1-α, it was revealed that the fungi collected resided in a distinct...

item.title: Protective effects of Gentiana macrophylla Pall. against blue light-induced retinal injury associated with of antioxidant defense, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, and inflammatory responses
item.description: CONCLUSION: MEG pretreatment attenuated acute BL-induced retinal injury, accompanied by changes in antioxidant defense-related markers, mitochondrial status, apoptosis-associated alterations, and inflammatory responses. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting further investigation of MEG as a potential protective botanical preparation against oxidative and phototoxic retinal injury.

item.title: Research Trends in the Journal of Dental Hygiene Science Using Keyword Network Analysis and Topic Modeling: A Comparative Study of Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Periods (2015∼2024)
item.description: CONCLUSION: Over the past decade, JDHS research has shifted from an education- and psychology-oriented focus to clinical and experimental studies, with infection control emerging as an independent research theme after COVID-19. However, internationally prominent topics such as teledentistry and digital dentistry remain underrepresented, suggesting the need for expanded research in these emerging areas. This study provides quantitative evidence of structural changes in Korean dental hygiene...

item.title: Research Trends in Artificial Intelligence Applications in Dental Hygiene and Dentistry in Korean Academic Journals: A Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: AI research in Korea exhibits divergent developmental trajectories. Dental hygiene research emphasizes education, prevention, and public oral health, combining exploratory and applied approaches, while dentistry demonstrates greater clinical integration and application-level maturity. Advancing AI maturity in dental hygiene will require expansion of clinical data-driven studies, incorporation of AI and data literacy into curricula, standardized integration of unstructured and...

item.title: Evaluating the Accuracy of an Artificial Intelligence Solution Program for Identifying Anatomical Landmarks in Orthodontics
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that EzOrtho may offer clinical utility and reliability for automatic cephalometric landmark detection using real clinical data. Its performance indicates the potential to improve efficiency and consistency relative to manual tracing. However, the study's limitations, including its small sample size, mean that these results remain preliminary. Further validation is needed to establish its role as a decision-support tool in orthodontic practice.

item.title: Periodontal ligament stem cells modulate macrophage inflammation in association with pyrimidine metabolic remodeling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PDLSCs modulate macrophage inflammation in association with coordinated remodeling of Pyrimidine metabolism. Functional studies with TAU further support a role for pyrimidine metabolic regulation in controlling inflammatory responses and tissue repair, highlighting this metabolic pathway as a potential therapeutic target for oral inflammatory diseases.

item.title: Development of a multidimensional scale for discomfort related to personal protective equipment and its exploratory association with musculoskeletal symptoms among Korean healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The PPE Discomfort Scale identified two dimensions: direct wearing burden and organisational vulnerability, supporting a multidimensional conceptualisation of PPE-related discomfort. In exploratory analyses, organisational vulnerability showed a stronger association with MSDs, although this association was attenuated after additional adjustment. Further studies are needed to confirm the factor structure and evaluate the scale in other healthcare settings.

item.title: Short-term dietary and exercise interventions modify the CD86-Faecalibaculum association linked to adipose tissue inflammation after prolonged high-fat diet exposure
item.description: CONCLUSION: The CD86-Faecalibaculum association was linked to AT inflammation and adverse metabolic measures after prolonged HFD exposure. Dietary reversal, particularly when combined with exercise, was associated with improved metabolic, immune, and microbial profiles.

item.title: Baseline and longitudinal changes in blood biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in pirfenidone-treated idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a prospective observational study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that several blood biomarkers, particularly CCL18, KL-6, and CA-125, may provide additional prognostic information for IPF patients receiving pirfenidone and warrant further investigation.

item.title: Estimation of serial intervals and time-varying reproduction numbers across SARS-CoV-2 variants in childcare clusters: symptom onset vs. reporting dates
item.description: CONCLUSION: The choice of temporal reference substantially affects SI and Rt estimation in childcare clusters. Reliance on reporting dates may underestimate real-time transmission intensity and distort epidemic risk assessment. Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.

item.title: Machine learning-based risk prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B: current evidence and future directions
item.description: CONCLUSION: ML-based models may complement conventional risk scores and support individualized surveillance in CHB. Future research should prioritize dynamic, multimodal, externally validated, and clinically implementable systems that improve surveillance decisions and patient outcomes.

item.title: Treatment burden and long-term morbidity after transoral robotic vs. nonrobotic surgery for oropharyngeal cancer
item.description: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) is widely used in the surgical management of oropharyngeal cancer, yet its longer-term consequences beyond survival and perioperative care remain uncertain. We examined 4,173 patients who underwent surgery for oropharyngeal cancer using nationwide Korean National Health Insurance Service data from 2010 to 2023. item.title: Genomic and Transcriptomic Changes in Early Gastric Cancer Inform Clinical Risk Stratification Prior to Endoscopic Resection
item.description: CONCLUSION: Integrating genomic and transcriptomic data with clinicopathologic features provides additional insight into the molecular characteristics associated with established risk categories in EGC. These findings expand our understanding of the molecular heterogeneity of EGC and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating the clinical utility of molecular profiling in larger independent cohorts.

item.title: Meta-Analysis: Moderate HBV DNA Levels Are Associated With the Highest Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Moderate HBV DNA levels were associated with the highest pooled HCC incidence across the predefined categories.

item.title: International expert perspectives on three-dimensional virtual hepatectomy: clinical value, selective use, and implementation barriers
item.description: CONCLUSION: Experts valued 3D virtual hepatectomy primarily for maintaining intraoperative orientation and guiding an appropriate transection plane with an adequate surgical margin. Selective, question-driven use and reduced reconstruction burden may support broader implementation.

item.title: Inflammatory and cardiometabolic signatures of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in rheumatoid arthritis: a machine learning analysis of NHANES 2003-2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Traditional cardiovascular factors remained dominant correlates of prevalent ASCVD in adults with RA. ABSI was the most consistent composite marker, whereas inflammatory indices showed model-dependent importance. Longitudinal validation is required before clinical use in RA populations.

item.title: Assessment of Potential Microplastic and Particulate Wear Debris Generation from Road-Marking Paint Wear in School Zones
item.description: This study developed a screening-level model to estimate the potential generation of microplastics and particulate wear debris from cold-plastic road markings in a hypothetical fully painted school zone (300 m × 6 m; 1,800 m²) in South Korea. Because published area-based wear data are averaged over the marked surface, they were applied to the total painted area rather than to a wheel-path sub-area. item.title: Redesigning the bacterial envelope: Multi-layered genetic strategies for outer membrane vesicle production
item.description: Bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are promising nanoplatforms for therapeutics, vaccines, and bioengineering; however, their industrial translation is constrained by low native yields and strain-dependent heterogeneity. Although static genetic knockouts can enhance vesicle shedding, they often provoke envelope fragility, premature cell lysis, and downstream contamination-creating a severe trade-off between vesicle yield and host cellular fitness. item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Thoracic Pathology and Biomarker Assessment: An IASLC Pathology Committee Review
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to transform pathology by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and therapeutic prediction through advanced computational analysis of histopathological images. This review explores key AI methodologies and their applications in lung cancer diagnostics. item.title: Prognostic Significance of AI-Quantified Central Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes in Bladder Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AI-based quantification of TILs at the tumor center was associated with favorable survival outcomes across two independent bladder cancer cohorts, whereas measurements at the invasive front showed no significant prognostic association. These findings support the potential prognostic relevance of spatially resolved TIL assessment in bladder cancer and warrant further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

item.title: Estrogen loss and Alzheimer's disease: five exposures ordered by age, and why timing is the variable to test
item.description: Alzheimer's disease occurs about twice as often in women as in men. A widely held hypothesis attributes part of the excess to loss of ovarian estradiol at menopause and, at its simplest, predicts that risk tracks the level of estrogen available to the brain. item.title: Adaptive Replanning in Hypofractionated Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Large Brain Metastases
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adaptive replanning based on early volumetric response was feasible during hypofractionated SRS for large BMs and was not associated with increased toxicity; however, a clinical benefit of replanning over non-adaptive treatment, including a reduction in radiation necrosis or transient swelling, was not demonstrated. Inter-fractional tumor volume reduction may serve as an early indicator of favorable local control.

item.title: Quality, Power, and Fragility of Randomized Controlled Trials in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis: A Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Most trials in AAV were of good quality, but were small, frequently underpowered, and highly fragile. A shift in the outcomes of only five participants on average, often fewer than the number of participants lost to follow-up, would have been sufficient to change findings.

item.title: Histone remodeling in immune cells and its metabolic regulation and implications for metabolic disease
item.description: Immune cells continuously adapt to local tissue environments, and this functional plasticity plays a critical role in tissue homeostasis and metabolic disease. Emerging evidence indicates that histone post-translational modifications (HPTMs) contribute to immune cell adaptation by linking metabolic and environmental signals to transcriptional regulation. Beyond canonical histone acetylation and methylation, recently characterized modifications, including lactylation, crotonylation, and...

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics uncovers pharmacokinetic and tumor-intrinsic determinants of resistance to trastuzumab deruxtecan in breast cancer
item.description: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is effective in both HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancers, but clinical responses are heterogeneous. To delineate spatial determinants of response, we perform spatial transcriptomics in patients treated with T-DXd. More spatially dispersed HER2 expression in cancer cells correlates with improved response, consistent with the bystander effect. item.description: The postmortem diagnosis of fatal hypothermia remains challenging, particularly when alcohol exposure complicates interpretation of β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB). item.title: Regional factors associated with social isolation and subjective cognitive decline among Korean older adults: A multilevel analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The association between social isolation and SCD was weaker in districts with more senior leisure facilities, with no evidence that this pattern differed between urban and rural areas. Community infrastructure that supports social engagement may help socially isolated older adults; longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these associations.

item.title: Employment patterns and correlates among young adults registered with autism or intellectual disability in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Educational experiences, caregiver-reported functioning, and family characteristics were associated with employment status. Cross-sectional data cannot establish temporal or causal direction and may partly reflect employment-related differences in caregiver ratings. Longitudinal studies with independent assessments are needed to clarify these relationships and inform support planning.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Post-diagnosis metformin use was associated with lower unadjusted mortality in patients with kidney cancer, but this association was likely inflated by immortal time bias and was not adjusted for tumor characteristics or other confounders. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in studies with time-varying exposure and detailed clinical data.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Routine dipstick results add a small increment to age, sex, and BMI for identifying serum urate ≥7.0 mg/dL. item.description: Chronic allograft injury and progressive loss of graft function remain major challenges after kidney transplantation. item.title: Risk of major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality across chronic kidney disease stages: A population-based retrospective cohort study in South Korea
item.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with increased cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk. However, few studies have assessed whether these risks vary across CKD stages in Asian populations. Using Korean National Health Insurance data (2016-2020), we analyzed a cohort of 51,352 individuals newly diagnosed with CKD. item.description: Despite the availability of measures to control hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related diseases, achieving elimination remains a substantial challenge. item.title: Clinical characteristics across graded frailty status in older public hospital outpatients: An exploratory cross-sectional study
item.description: Frailty is a multidimensional geriatric syndrome, but practical clinical indicators that reflect vulnerability across graded frailty status in routine outpatient care remain insufficiently characterized. This exploratory cross-sectional study included 28 community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older who attended outpatient clinics at a public hospital in Seoul, Republic of Korea. item.title: Comparing outcomes of trigger finger release in patients with and without diabetes mellitus: A meta-analysis
item.description: Diabetes increases the risk of developing trigger digits and may predispose patients to poorer clinical outcomes and a higher incidence of complications. item.title: Comparison of claims-defined postpartum depression after cesarean delivery under spinal versus epidural anesthesia: A nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study in Korea
item.description: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common and serious mental health disorder that adversely affects maternal well-being and early parenting. Although spinal and epidural anesthesia are widely used during cesarean section, their differential associations with PPD remain unclear. This nationwide retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service between 2013 and 2022. Women who underwent cesarean section with either spinal or epidural anesthesia were included....

item.description: Background This study aimed to evaluate the association between the Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI) and the Fatty Liver Index (FLI), both serving as surrogate indices of hepatic steatosis, and breast cancer risk among Korean women. Methods This nationwide cohort study included 3,629,375 women aged ≥40 years who participated in a national breast cancer screening program between 2009 and 2010. item.description: To counter the environmental issues, recently hydrogen has emerged as a substitute candidate for fossil fuels which can produce via electrolysis of the water requiring efficient electrocatalyst. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in this study. Younger patients exhibited greater pharmacokinetic variability, necessitating closer monitoring and cautious dose adjustment. Prospective PK-PD studies incorporating standardized clinical outcomes are needed to define optimal trough targets and individualized dosing strategies.

item.title: Sustained reduction of blood culture contamination with a dedicated phlebotomy team
item.description: Blood culture contamination and inadequate fill volumes compromise the diagnosis of bloodstream infections. While dedicated phlebotomy teams improve these metrics, evidence regarding long-term sustainability is scarce. We evaluated the impact of a 24/7 dedicated phlebotomy team on blood culture quality using a 9-year longitudinal data set. item.title: Sex-disaggregated pooled serious injury prevalence among school-going adolescents aged 13-17 years across 44 Global School-based Student Health Survey datasets, 2015-2023: a meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Across the included national GSHS surveys, serious injury was common among school-going adolescents aged 13-17 years, with a numerically higher pooled prevalence among male individuals. The findings support the need for context- and sex-specific injury prevention strategies in schools, including, where relevant, road safety measures, violence and bullying prevention, and stronger adolescent injury surveillance.

item.title: The Role and Significance of Oxidative Stress in Inflammatory Periodontal Disease and Contemporary Approaches to Antioxidant Therapy
item.description: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by dysbiotic biofilms and an exaggerated host immune response, resulting in progressive destruction of periodontal tissues and tooth loss. Increasing evidence suggests that oxidative and nitrosative stress play central roles in disease progression by amplifying inflammation, promoting tissue damage, and impairing repair mechanisms. item.title: Analytical Quality by Design Approach for the Optimization and Validation of a Robust RP-HPLC Method for Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid in a Finished Product
item.description: The amoxicillin/clavulanic acid combination, widely used in oral antibacterial therapy, requires analytical methods that are robust, reliable, and suitable for lifecycle management. item.title: Disease Modeling of Fabry Disease Cardiomyopathy using Base Editing-Established Isogenic iPSCs and Application of Prime Editing for Gene Correction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that base-edited isogenic hiPSC-CMs provide a personalized platform for evaluating therapeutic efficacy without patient-derived samples. Moreover, genetic correction of GLA via prime editing highlights the potential of gene therapy for FD.

item.title: Enhanced oral care interventions for preventing postoperative pneumonia in patients with esophageal cancer: A scoping review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: As pneumonia is associated with poor clinical outcomes in patients with esophageal cancer, oral care may be considered an important preventive measure. Standardized oral care guidelines and consistent oral hygiene management should be implemented throughout the entire course of treatment.

item.title: Spatial iris chromaticity disparities as phenotypic correlates of harm avoidance temperament in a Korean sample
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The human iris has a complex developmental origin, with neural crest-derived cells contributing to the formation of the iris stroma and its melanocyte population. Although ocular visual features have been linked to personality traits in Western cohorts, whether quantitative spatial chromaticity disparities in the iris are associated with temperament dimensions in Korean individuals remains understudied.

item.description: Subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is being explored as a device-based option for obesity, but translation is limited by the lack of standardized implantation workflows and cuff electrodes that remain stable at the cuff-nerve interface in a moist in vivo environment. item.title: Short-, medium- and long-term sequelae following COVID-19 infection: a network cohort study across multiple Asia-Pacific regions
item.description: BACKGROUND: Existing evidence on post-COVID-19 sequelae were largely derived from single-database studies among western population with limited generalizability. This multi-regional study aimed to characterize the risk of clinical sequelae across multiple organ systems over short- (0-90 days), medium- (91-365 days) and long-term (>365 days) phases following SARS-CoV-2 infection among the Asia-Pacific population.

item.title: Microscope-Integrated Quantitative Fluorescence Imaging for Assessing Crack Severity in Teeth
item.description: CONCLUSION: The microscope-QLF hybrid technique showed a measurable and consistent relationship with QLF-D for quantitative fluorescence assessment. Although systematic differences were observed, the hybrid technique may serve as a supportive tool for assessing relative crack severity during endodontic procedures.

item.title: Comparative Evaluation of Plaque Visualization-Based Digital Oral Health Education Media Among Pregnant Women in Vietnam: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Perceived educational values and preferences varied by digital oral health education medium. Although video-based education was preferred for accessibility and initial understanding, plaque visualization-based mobile application education received higher ratings for supporting self-management and feedback. These findings indicate that alcohol-free EO rinses may be a clinically useful alternative for patients who cannot tolerate alcohol-containing products or long-term CHX use. item.description: CONCLUSION: The spatial distribution of dental healthcare institutions in Korea has exhibited a gradual trend toward greater equilibrium over time. item.title: Post-Synthetic Ligand Modification of a MOF-74 Analogue via Criss-Cross Cycloaddition of Azine Linkages With Isocyanates for Toluene Removal
item.description: Modifying the pore environment of MOF-74-type frameworks remains challenging because existing functionalization strategies often suffer from limited versatility, poor reproducibility, or compromised structural stability. item.title: Contralateral Preauricular Free Flap Reconstruction After Wide Excision of Recurrent Congenital Preauricular Sinus
item.description: Recurrent congenital preauricular sinus after previous treatment may require wide excision of scarred and inflamed tissue, leaving a skin defect with underlying dead space. We reviewed 7 referred patients (mean age, 16.4 y) who underwent wide excision and immediate contralateral preauricular free flap reconstruction from 2021 to 2025. item.title: Giant Pleomorphic Lipoma of the Occipital Scalp Mimicking Well-Differentiated Liposarcoma
item.description: Pleomorphic lipoma is a rare, benign adipocytic tumor within the spindle cell lipoma spectrum that typically arises in the subcutaneous tissue of the posterior neck, shoulder, or upper back of older men. We report an exceptional case of giant pleomorphic lipoma arising in the occipital scalp of a 63-year-old woman, presenting as a slowly enlarging mass over ~3 years. item.title: Subjective Cognitive Decline-Related Functional Limitations and Suicidal Ideation Among Korean Older Adults: The Indirect Role of Depressive Symptoms and the Moderating Role of Living Alone
item.description: Using data from the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey, this study examined whether subjective cognitive decline (SCD)-related functional limitations were indirectly associated with suicidal ideation (SI) through depressive symptoms and whether this association differed by living arrangement among 26,552 adults reporting worsening confusion or memory loss. item.title: Maternal obesity and risk of congenital heart disease in offspring: a nationwide population-based study
item.description: Maternal obesity is a well-established risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its association with congenital heart disease (CHD) in offspring remains uncertain, particularly across different body mass index (BMI) categories and CHD subtypes. Evidence from Asian populations is limited, despite distinct BMI distributions and classification criteria. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Information Database, including 779,091 live births...

item.title: Enzymatic apoplast release enables rapid, reproducible isolation of plant small EVs from Arabidopsis young seedlings
item.description: Recently, interest in plant extracellular vesicles (EVs) has grown alongside increasing demand for standardized isolation methods. In this study, we present the enzyme method (E method) for isolating small EVs from Arabidopsis seedlings to study EV biomarkers and functions. The E method highlights gentle cell wall digestion for rapid isolation and yields a concentration of small EVs within the 50-150 nm size range. item.title: Cost-utility analysis of HPV-cytology co-testing in the Korean national cervical cancer screening program
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that biennial cytology remains economically efficient under current Korean conditions and that the addition of HPV testing would not be cost-effective at the present WTP threshold. Reconsideration may be warranted if HPV testing costs decrease substantially.

item.title: Guideline-practice gap in molecular subtyping and lynch syndrome screening for endometrial cancer
item.description: CONCLUSION: Molecular classification remains limited by factors that likely reflect financial and institutional barriers restricting POLE testing, although its clinical utility was demonstrated by de-escalation of radiotherapy in a POLE-mutated patient. Similarly, the absence of MLH1 methylation triage renders Lynch syndrome screening non-selective, lowering germline testing completion rates. item.title: Twenty-five-year trends and projections of gynecologic cancer incidence in Korea: findings from cancer registry data
item.description: CONCLUSION: The burden of corpus uteri and ovarian cancers is expected to increase substantially, highlighting the need for effective prevention and management strategies.

item.title: Intralesional triamcinolone plus gentamicin versus triamcinolone alone for keloid: a two-center cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adding gentamicin to intralesional TAC was associated with greater scar improvement, but treatment was confounded with site of care; randomized confirmation is required before clinical adoption.

item.title: Nursing Workload Distribution and Its Association With Patient Safety Culture in Tertiary and General Hospitals: A Focus on Ward Models
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patient safety culture was associated with certain hospital/ward types and perceived staffing adequacy, whereas no clear association was observed with self-reported nursing-time allocation. These findings suggest that patient safety culture extends beyond nursing-time distribution alone.

item.title: Artificial intelligence in periodontitis: current evidence, clinical limitations, and research priorities
item.description: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in periodontology are expanding faster than the evidence supporting their clinical use. Beyond radiographic bone-loss detection and quantification, these applications include oral-image screening, risk prediction using electronic dental records, longitudinal progression modeling, treatment-response prediction, and models based on biomarkers, the microbiome, or gene expression.
